messages:
Maya: Quick sync — FinCorp POC kickoff next Wed. They want guaranteed latency and predictable cost. Can we agree on a realistic acceptance matrix (latency R95/p95, cost per 1k tokens, quality pass rate)?
Ben: What traffic shape are we designing for? RPS, % long queries?
Olivia: From pre-call: peak 200 RPS, avg ~60 RPS. Distribution: short <=64 tokens 40%, medium 64-512 50%, long >512 10%. Spiky concurrency (lots of bursts).
Jordan: For 200 RPS peak we should use a dedicated GPU pool + autoscale. With batching + KV cache we can expect p95: short ~180–250ms, medium ~350–500ms. Long queries need async or higher tail allowance (~1.2s). Fallback to smaller model at high queue depths.
Maya: FinCorp asked for p95 <300ms for production traffic. Is that realistic?
Ben: Short/medium yes if we pin model and prewarm. But overall p95 <300ms is tight given 10% long queries. Suggested acceptance: p95(short+medium) <=350ms, p95(overall) <=450ms with explicit long-query SLAs or async doc jobs.
Aisha: Quality side — they do legal summarization. Propose automated eval + human spot-check. Automated threshold: ROUGE-L >= 0.6 and embedding-similarity >= 0.85 on a 300-prompt set. Human spot-check pass rate >=92% on 30 samples. Also monitor hallucination rate; reject if >5% regressions.
Maya: Cost — they want predictability. Any rough $/1k token guidance for dedicated vs hosted?
Jordan: Ballpark: dedicated with quantized large model (Llama2-style) effective infra cost ~ $0.30–0.60 / 1k tokens depending on batching and KV hit rate. Hosted smaller model variants can be around $0.08–0.20 / 1k tokens. We'll provide a formal quote but recommend a short committed capacity for the POC to hit their cost target.
Ben: Caching will matter. Prefix/KV cache can cut token spend 20–40% for repeated prompts. Also suggest request-level batching where latency budget allows.
Olivia: POC timeline proposal (2 weeks):
- Day 0–1: infra prep, KMS + VPC checks, provisioning.
- Day 2–4: smoke tests at 50 RPS, validate latencies and fallback.
- Day 5–10: run eval harness (300 prompts x 3 runs), collect metrics and error cases.
- Day 11–13: customer UAT with real traffic slice.
- Day 14: acceptance review and handoff.
Maya: Security checklist — FinCorp requires KMS, audit logs, and EU data residency (eu-west-1). Can we do that for Dedicated/Private?
Jordan: Yes. Dedicated and Private support KMS, audit logs, and region pinning. For Hosted we can offer region-limited endpoints but for strict residency they should choose Dedicated/Private. If they need HSM-backed keys we can integrate their PKI (extra setup).
Aisha: I'll assemble the eval prompt set focused on legal clauses + adversarial cases. Example prompts (preview):
```
[
  {"id": "p1", "prompt": "Summarize the indemnity clause in plain English."},
  {"id": "p2", "prompt": "Extract all obligations for the vendor from this contract snippet."},
  {"id": "p3", "prompt": "Flag potential liability language and suggested mitigations."}
]
```
Ben: Eval harness snippet (pseudo):
```bash
# run evals locally against staging endpoint
python run_eval.py --endpoint https://staging.redwood/api/v1/generate --input eval_prompts.json --runs 3 --metrics rouge,embed_sim,hallucination_rate
```
Olivia: Add monitoring: per-route p50/p95/p99, token burn, KV cache hit rate, and quality drift alerts (daily). We'll attach a dashboard template.
deploy-bot: Provisioning dedicated-gpu-pool for fincorp-poc — ETA ~3h. Instance group: rdw-poc-XX.
Maya: :thumbsup: Thanks. Next steps: Ben + Olivia deliver eval harness and sample metrics dashboard by EOD tomorrow. Jordan to confirm cost ranges and KMS architecture (include HSM note). Aisha to share 300-prompt set. I'll sync with FinCorp on acceptance matrix and proposed timeline.
Ben: On it.
Olivia: I'll upload the sample eval set and dashboard link to the shared drive after this thread.
Jordan: I'll send the capacity/cost table and KMS/HSM integration steps in a separate doc by EOD.
Aisha: Preparing the adversarial prompts now — will include edge cases and red-team items.
Maya: Good plan. If we can get a quick demo that shows <350ms for the 80% common paths, that should placate their procurement. Thanks team.
